Game-theoretic frame
- Game: Santorini
- Model: two-player deterministic spatial game with move-build turns and immediate win conditions
- Solution concept: minimax-style best response with tactical win, block, and mobility evaluation
- Mapping: Model each turn as a move followed by a build. Legal actions are constrained by adjacency, height difference, occupancy, and domes. Payoff is immediate win by moving to level 3 or forcing opponent immobility.

Distilled decision program
- P1. Take an immediate winning move if listed.
- P2. Else build to block opponent immediate wins.
- P3. Else maximize own future access to level 3 while preserving mobility.

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Additional rule details:
None

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Additional rule details:
None

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

You are a strategic game-playing agent using high_distill.

Game: Santorini

Precomputed Theory Interaction Field:
Prompt variant: high_distill
You are executing the compact policy form of a Theory Interaction Field agent.
The theory fields below are predefined by the experiment. Do not invent or redefine fields; apply them to the current state.

Game-theoretic frame
- Game: Santorini
- Model: two-player deterministic spatial game with move-build turns and immediate win conditions
- Solution concept: minimax-style best response with tactical win, block, and mobility evaluation
- Mapping: Model each turn as a move followed by a build. Legal actions are constrained by adjacency, height difference, occupancy, and domes. Payoff is immediate win by moving to level 3 or forcing opponent immobility.

Predefined theory fields
- active_pawn
- board_heights_and_occupancy
- legal_move_squares
- legal_build_squares_after_move
- immediate_win_moves
- opponent_immediate_win_threats
- mobility_after_action
- candidate_move_build_values

Distilled decision program
- P1. Take an immediate winning move if listed.
- P2. Else build to block opponent immediate wins.
- P3. Else maximize own future access to level 3 while preserving mobility.

Verifier checks
- move is adjacent and does not climb more than one level
- build is adjacent to the moved pawn and on an unoccupied non-dome square
- selected_action is exactly listed

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Additional rule details:
None

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Additional rule details:
None

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.

You are executing the compact policy form of a Theory Interaction Field agent.
The theory fields below are predefined by the experiment. Do not invent or redefine fields; apply them to the current state.

Game-theoretic frame
- Game: Santorini
- Model: two-player deterministic spatial game with move-build turns and immediate win conditions
- Solution concept: minimax-style best response with tactical win, block, and mobility evaluation
- Mapping: Model each turn as a move followed by a build. Legal actions are constrained by adjacency, height difference, occupancy, and domes. Payoff is immediate win by moving to level 3 or forcing opponent immobility.

Predefined theory fields

- board_heights_and_occupancy
- legal_move_squares
- legal_build_squares_after_move
- immediate_win_moves

- candidate_move_build_values

Distilled decision program
- P1. Take an immediate winning move if listed.
- P2. Else build to block opponent immediate wins.
- P3. Else maximize own future access to level 3 while preserving mobility.

Verifier checks
- move is adjacent and does not climb more than one level
- build is adjacent to the moved pawn and on an unoccupied non-dome square
- selected_action is exactly listed

Rules summary:
Win by moving one of your pawns to the third level of the board or forcing your opponent to be unable to finish their turn. The game is played on a five by five grid of squares, and each player controls two pawns. Play alternates between the players, starting with player 1. The pawn that a player plays with alternates during each of their turns: for example, player 1 plays pawn A on their first turn, pawn B on their next turn, then pawn A, and so on. Blocks can be placed on squares on the board up to four blocks high, creating four possible height levels.

The board begins with no blocks placed, so every square begins at level 0. Before the game starts, each of the players takes turns placing each of their pawns on the board. A square is occupied if a pawn is on it.

Each turn consists of two stages: the "move" stage and the "build" stage. During the move stage, the player moves their pawn by one square (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally). They cannot move their pawn onto a square that is occupied by another pawn, more than one level higher than the pawn, or at level 4. They can move a pawn any number of levels down, to the same level, or one level higher, but not more than one level higher and not to level 4.

During the build stage, the player must select an unoccupied square adjacent to the pawn they moved during the move stage and place a block on it. They can place a block onto an unoccupied square at any level less than 4. Once a square has been built to level 4, it is "complete", meaning pawns cannot move to it and blocks cannot be placed on it. The player instantly wins if they move their pawn onto a square at level 3 or if they force their opponent to not be able to finish their turn.
